D2.quote: Wipes fields not present in the body. `t.Due = due` and `t.Tags = req.Tags` run unconditionally, so `PATCH {"title":"y"}` erases the task's existing due date and tags. Violates "fields not present in the body keep their values."
D2.evidence: go test ./... -run Repro -v → "due wiped by unrelated PATCH: got \"0001-01-01\"" and "tags wiped by unrelated PATCH: got []"

D3.quote: `CreatedAt` is dropped. The new `Task{}` never copies `o.Created`, so migrated tasks lose their creation time, contradicting "every task keeps its ... creation time."
D3.evidence: go test ./... -run Repro -v → "CreatedAt lost during migration: {... CreatedAt:0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC}"

D4.quote: v1 labels aren't normalized. `strings.Split(o.Labels, ",")` skips trim/lowercase/max-5, so migrated tags don't follow "the same rules as in create."
D4.evidence: go test ./... -run Repro -v → "migrated tags not normalized: [ Home   Urgent ]"

D5.quote: Due-today tasks show as overdue. Same check doesn't exclude `Due == today`; spec requires "before today."
D5.evidence: go test ./... -run Repro -v → "task due today shown as overdue: [{ID:t0001 Title:due today Done:false Due:2026-03-10 00:00:00 +0000 UTC ...}]"

D6.quote: No-due-date tasks show as overdue. The exclusion check `t.Due.After(today.Time)` treats the zero-value `Date{}` (year 1) as "not after today," so tasks with no due date incorrectly appear when `overdue=true`.
D6.evidence: go test ./... -run Repro -v → "task with no due date shown as overdue: [{ID:t0001 Title:no due date Done:false Due:0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC ...}]"

D7.quote: Tags aren't normalized. `t.Tags = req.Tags` skips `normalizeTags`, so PATCH lets tags in with whitespace/mixed case and bypasses the max-5 check — inconsistent with create and breaks the case-insensitive tag filter.
D7.evidence: go test ./... -run Repro -v → "PATCH tags not normalized: [ Work  URGENT]"

D8.quote: Unknown id returns 204, not 404. `Store.Delete` silently no-ops on a missing key and never surfaces `ErrNotFound`, so the handler always returns 204.
D8.evidence: go test ./... -run Repro -v → "delete unknown id: got 204, want 404"

D9.quote: Malformed JSON body doesn't 400. The decode error is discarded (`json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)`), so `PATCH` with invalid JSON returns 200 instead of 400.
D9.evidence: go test ./... -run Repro -v → "malformed PATCH body: got 200, want 400"
